documents.text:
# Maker Hall membership handbook

This handbook is an original fictional fixture for software testing. Maker Hall is not a real customer. The membership desk keeps a paper backup of essential notices.

## Visitors and induction
A first-time visitor may tour the workshop with a host. Visitors must not operate power tools until they finish the safety induction. Booking a tour does not count as completing induction. An inducted member may use the hand-tool benches without an appointment when a supervisor is present.

## Access cards
When a member loses an access card, the desk disables the missing card immediately and issues a replacement after checking the membership number. Replacement cards cost 12 credits. A card found later must be returned; it must not be reactivated. The desk can lend a day pass while the new card is prepared.

## Membership pauses
A member can pause a subscription for at least two full weeks by telling the desk before the next billing date. The pause begins on the next billing date, not on the day the member asks. The desk does not backdate pauses. Members who need a shorter break can keep their normal membership active.

## Closing routine
The last supervisor checks the soldering irons, shuts the windows and records unfinished repairs in the shift notebook. Members leave borrowed tools on the inspection bench rather than putting them straight back into storage.

documents.name: equipment-service.txt
documents.text:
Equipment maintenance register

This is an invented register for a fictional shared workshop, not manufacturer advice.

EX-1049: The amber bench lamp flickers after ten minutes. Keep this lamp unplugged until the replacement adapter arrives. Inspection is scheduled for Wednesday morning. The lamp's repair ticket is MT-4821.

EX-1094: The blue bench lamp passed its electrical inspection on Monday. This lamp is available for normal use. Its inspection ticket is MT-4281. Do not confuse EX-1094 with EX-1049.

The laser cutter's extraction fan must run whenever the cutter is active. If smoke remains inside the enclosure after a job, stop the machine and call the supervisor. Cleaning the lid is not a substitute for checking the extraction filter.

To borrow a cordless drill overnight, sign the tool-out sheet before closing. Bring the drill and both batteries back by 10:00 the following morning. The charger stays at the workshop and is not included in an overnight loan.

The 3D printer uses blue PLA for public demonstrations. A tangled filament spool goes in the repair tray; do not throw it in ordinary waste. The weekly maintenance routine includes checking the nozzle and wiping dust from the enclosure.

Spare adapters are stored in drawer B-17. Drawer B-71 contains printed manuals, not adapters. The two labels are deliberately similar for identifier-sensitive search.

documents.name: supplier-returns.md
documents.text:
# Supplier returns and refunds

This is an invented policy for a fictional workshop shop. All amounts use fictional credits. It is not legal or financial advice.

## Faulty products
A customer who receives a faulty unopened tool can ask for a replacement or a refund within thirty days of collection. Record the receipt number and the reported fault. A photograph is useful but is not mandatory when the customer can bring the item to the desk.

## Custom orders
Custom engraved items are not refundable merely because a customer changes their mind. This does not remove the replacement or refund route for a manufacturing defect. Staff should read the fault report before deciding which policy applies.

## Refund handling
A refund goes back to the original payment method. Desk staff must not issue a cash refund for an item originally paid by bank transfer. If the original method is unavailable, refer the case to the coordinator rather than selecting an alternative without approval.

## Packaging and transit
If a parcel arrives with a crushed outer box, keep the packaging until the supplier responds. The transport claim needs the delivery date, order number and photographs of the damage. A damaged box by itself is not evidence that the tool inside is faulty.

## Receipt identifiers
Receipt RC-00731 concerns an unopened soldering iron returned for a manufacturing defect. Receipt RC-00713 concerns an engraved sign collected without a fault report. The receipt numbers refer to different orders.

documents.name: room-bookings.md
documents.text:
# Room bookings

These are original fictional room-booking instructions created only for evaluation. The workshop has a quiet classroom and a noisy fabrication room.

## Moving a booking
A member who cannot attend a booked class may move the booking once if they contact the desk at least twenty-four hours before the class begins. Moving a booking later than that requires the coordinator's approval. A member may transfer a place to another inducted member instead.

## Quiet room
The quiet classroom closes at 19:30 on Fridays. The fabrication room remains open until 21:00 when a trained supervisor is present. Friday opening times are different from weekday opening times.

## Group sessions
A group must nominate one host who stays until every visitor leaves. The host checks that borrowed chairs are returned and writes missing equipment in the shift notebook. The real process might store a contact number, but this fixture deliberately contains no contact details.

## Cancellations
A class cancelled by the workshop receives a full booking-credit refund. A member who simply fails to attend does not receive an automatic refund. The coordinator may review exceptional cases individually.
